comment: GCN 2651 reports the ESO-VLT I-band observation on 2004-08-12.9795 UT (first epoch; it also reports Aug 13.9844 UT), ten 60-s exposures per epoch, and an initial approximate full-field limit I~24. The circular does not define whether its UT anchor is an exposure start or midpoint; the reported first-epoch UT is retained as the time anchor. D’Avanzo+2007 reanalyzed these same epochs: the Chandra afterglow position was behind the occulting bar but visible in 2/10 dithered frames in each epoch, and a coincident optical source faded significantly. Thus I~24 is not a valid afterglow upper limit and this preliminary row is discarded. The paper gives no tabulated per-point magnitude/error/time; Figure 1 is not digitized. Magnitude system not declared in GCN 2651, mag_system left blank. Re-verified 2026-11-03 against gcn/archive/2651.json and the D'Avanzo arXiv v1 narrative (occulting bar, 2/10 dithered frames).

GCN 2643 reports VLA observation at 2004-08-14.15 UT; duration and whether this anchor is start/midpoint are unspecified, so time_err is left blank. This is the 4.9-GHz component at RA 16:26:08.5, Dec -44:41:04, flux 0.79 mJy. GCN 2643 gives beta~ -1, inconsistent with early radio afterglows; GCN 2648 reports no X-ray source at this VLA position. The source is not the fading Chandra #2 afterglow (GCN 2655; D’Avanzo+2007); preserve the reported measurement but discard it from the GRB afterglow light curve.

GCN 2643 reports VLA observation at 2004-08-14.15 UT; duration and whether this anchor is start/midpoint are unspecified, so time_err is left blank. Correct band is 8.5 GHz (the original 85GHz was a transcription error); flux is 0.45 mJy at RA 16:26:08.5, Dec -44:41:04. GCN 2643 gives beta~ -1, inconsistent with early radio afterglows; GCN 2648 reports no X-ray source at this VLA position. The source is not the fading Chandra #2 afterglow (GCN 2655; D’Avanzo+2007); preserve the reported measurement but discard it from the GRB afterglow light curve.

GCN 2643 same-epoch nondetection: 'No other sources are detected within the error box with a 2 sigma detection limit of 0.14 and 0.16 mJy at 4.9 and 8.5 GHz, respectively.' The 2-arcmin INTEGRAL error box contains the afterglow (Chandra source #2, GCN 2648/2655), so this image detection limit applies at the afterglow position as a 2-sigma upper limit; the detected 0.79 mJy VLA source is at a different position and is not the afterglow (see its discarded rows). Observation anchored at 2004-08-14.15 UT as reported; start/midpoint and integration duration unspecified, so time_err is left blank.

GCN 2653 reports this 1.28-GHz source #2 (RA 16:26:15.674, Dec -44:43:56.2; 2.5 mJy) among five previously uncatalogued field sources in a 15-arcmin GMRT field on Aug 16. GCN 2653 explicitly says no detectable emission at the VLA-source location. This coordinate is not the fading Chandra #2 afterglow in GCN 2648/2655. GCN 2655 says GMRT field sources #2 and #4 had the same flux level in both Chandra epochs; retain source measurement but discard as unrelated field emission. GCN 2653 gives date only; time is the calendar-date midpoint with ±12 h date precision, not an exposure midpoint.

GCN 2653 reports this 1.28-GHz source #1 (RA 16:26:08.404, Dec -44:41:27.2; 0.8 mJy) among five previously uncatalogued field sources in a 15-arcmin GMRT field on Aug 16. GCN 2653 says it lies within 2 arcsec of Chandra source #4 and explicitly says no detectable emission at the VLA-source location. GCN 2655 reports Chandra #4 stable between epochs; the likely fading afterglow is Chandra #2 at a different position. Retain source measurement but discard as unrelated field emission. GCN 2653 gives date only; time is the calendar-date midpoint with ±12 h date precision, not an exposure midpoint.
